heart.name: Diagonal Earlobe Crease (Frank's Sign)
heart.description: A diagonal crease running from the tragus to the outer edge of the earlobe at a 45° angle.
heart.why: Associated with poor circulation and atherosclerosis affecting small blood vessels.

heart.name: Arcus Senilis (Eye Ring)
heart.description: A white, gray, or blue arc or ring around the outer edge of the cornea.
heart.why: In people under 45, this ring may indicate high cholesterol linked to heart disease.

heart.name: Xanthelasma (Eyelid Deposits)
heart.description: Yellowish, flat or slightly raised deposits on the upper or lower eyelids.
heart.why: These are cholesterol deposits under the skin, a risk marker for heart disease.

heart.name: Peripheral Edema (Swollen Ankles)
heart.description: Abnormal swelling in the lower legs, ankles, or feet that leaves a pit when pressed.
heart.why: Can indicate heart failure where the heart is not pumping blood efficiently.

heart.name: Nail Clubbing
heart.description: Fingertips enlarge and nails curve downward, resembling an upside-down spoon.
heart.why: Associated with chronic low oxygen levels, which can indicate heart or lung disease.

kidney.name: Periorbital Edema (Puffy Eyes)
kidney.description: Swelling and puffiness around the eyes, especially noticeable in the morning.
kidney.why: Kidneys failing to filter protein cause fluid and protein to leak, leading to facial swelling.

kidney.name: Half-and-Half Nails (Lindsay's Nails)
kidney.description: The lower half of the nail appears white and the upper half appears brown or pink.
kidney.why: A classic sign of chronic kidney disease affecting nail pigmentation.

kidney.name: Pale Conjunctiva
kidney.description: The inner lining of the lower eyelid is pale pink or white instead of healthy red.
kidney.why: Kidney disease causes anemia, reducing red blood cells, making tissues appear pale.

kidney.name: Severe Ankle Edema
kidney.description: Significant bilateral swelling of the ankles and lower legs that is worse by evening.
kidney.why: Kidneys failing to regulate fluid cause sodium and water retention leading to edema.

kidney.name: Uremic Frost
kidney.description: White or yellowish crystal deposits visible on the skin surface, especially forehead.
kidney.why: In severe kidney failure, urea crystallizes on the skin as the body tries to excrete waste.

liver.name: Jaundice (Yellow Eyes/Skin)
liver.description: Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes (scleral icterus).
liver.why: A damaged liver cannot process bilirubin, causing it to build up and turn tissue yellow.

liver.name: Palmar Erythema (Red Palms)
liver.description: Redness of the palms, particularly the outer edges (thenar and hypothenar areas).
liver.why: Liver disease causes hormonal changes that dilate blood vessels in the palms.

liver.name: Spider Angiomas
liver.description: Small spider-like blood vessel formations visible on the face, chest, or hands.
liver.why: Excess estrogen from liver dysfunction causes small blood vessel abnormalities.

liver.name: Terry's Nails (White Nails)
liver.description: Nails appear mostly white with only a narrow pink or brown band at the tip.
liver.why: Associated with cirrhosis and other severe liver conditions affecting nail vascularity.

liver.name: Hepatic Fetor (Distinctive Breath)
liver.description: A distinctive musty, sweet, or fecal smell on the breath (cannot be photographed).
liver.why: Liver failure causes toxic compounds like dimethyl sulfide to be excreted through the lungs.
